You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Enabling timing-driven net weighting is the baseline-most lever (P-L1) and is currently off; turning it on with the default `adam`-style scheme lets the analytical placer pull critical nets together more strongly, which should reduce many moderate violations (TNS) across all circuits without changing partition/legality.

  bp-ng45: score=+0.140 dWNS=+12.2% dTNS=+15.0% overflow~111
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.090 dWNS=+9.4% dTNS=+8.7% overflow~103
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: all three cases are valid and improve, with dWNS and dTNS both positive (e.g., ariane133-ng45 +19.2%/+19.3%, bp-ng45 +12.2%/+15.0%, bp_fe-ng45 +9.4%/+8.7%), consistent with timing-driven net weighting pulling critical nets together and reducing moderate violations without legality issues. Overflow remains nonzero (~103–146), so congestion is a secondary concern. Next step: sweep the net-weighting strength/`adam` parameters and confirm overflow stays bounded, then check whether gains persist at higher utilization.
